## Purpose and Scope

This document is the design layer of the SDBS project. Its siblings cover
the other layers: the index describes the build system as it exists today,
the single-path artifact pipeline observation describes the production
side, and the living corpus document describes the knowledge-base domain
and its vision. This document sits between the vision and the code. It
states the target architecture for the next stage, records the design
decisions that are already made, and lists the questions that remain open.
It does not specify interfaces or data formats in code form.

The design is renderer-agnostic and substrate-agnostic in the same sense as
the build system: the corpus chain and its projections apply to any corpus
that the engine can validate and publish.

## Design Position

The project evolves along two layers that share one substrate and one
record model.

The engine layer is open. It validates, heals, renders, and extracts the
machine-readable corpus, and it declares what the current corpus is. Its
output is a canonical snapshot, deterministic and re-derivable by anyone.

The product layer observes accumulated snapshots. It owns the
observation-time responsibilities: the derived projections, the insight
paths woven across them, and the provenance and gap responses attached to
each path. It is a separate operating layer with its own boundary,
distinct from the build engine.

The boundary between the layers is explicit. The engine owns the build
time: validation, normalization, and snapshot declaration. The product
owns the observation time: projections, path weaving, and next-step
responses. Folding observation responsibilities into the build engine
would pull the project back toward a document builder with retrieval
bolted on.

## The Oracle Contract

An oracle is defined by four guarantees. The guarantees apply to the
insight paths it returns and separate an oracle from an index-driven
search engine.

- Determinism: the same snapshot and the same observation request produce
  the same path with the same evidence per hop.
- Provenance: every hop of a path carries the document, section, and cell
  it comes from.
- Freshness: every path states which corpus build it is bound to.
- Gap awareness: when the corpus contains no evidence for a path, the
  oracle returns an open intent instead of fabricating a step.

An oracle response is a path, and each hop is anchored to a fact with a
coordinate. Indexed search is the single-hop case of the same form.

The first gate for these guarantees is the snapshot contract. Every build
produces a corpus manifest with content-derived fingerprints, one per
document and one for the corpus as a whole. The manifest is the authority
that binds every observation to a specific corpus state.

## Structural Observation

The oracle observes the structure of the corpus for the task an agent
needs to perform and weaves the key insight paths that lead from the task
to the next step.
Each path crosses the derived projections: a structural hop to the section
that defines a term, a semantic hop to the document that develops it, a
temporal hop to the build that changed it, a relational hop to the
specification that constrains it, and a status hop that marks it as
superseded. Every hop carries provenance.

Path endpoints are next steps. A path that reaches a concrete directive or
a validated fact proposes that directive or fact as the next action. A
path that ends without evidence returns an open intent: the gap itself is
the next step, and the observation loop continues when new facts thicken
the structure. Agents deposit facts, the structure grows, and later
observations find richer paths.

## The Deterministic Primitive: a Single Canonical Chain

The organizing insight of the design is that a corpus of any complexity and
any document count can be represented as one stretched chain of ordered
cells. The chain is the primitive source. Every other structure, the
document hierarchy, the cross-reference graph, the time index, and the
semantic index, is a deterministic derived projection over the chain.

The chain has four properties.

A cell is the atomic unit. What a cell holds is an open question, recorded
below. Candidates are a token, a sentence, or a segment. Each cell carries
a structural coordinate, a content fingerprint, and, under a pinned model,
a deterministic vector.

Content is stored once. A unit that is included or referenced by many
documents exists at one coordinate, and documents refer to it instead of
duplicating it. A document is a coordinate interval, not a copy.

The order is canonical. The chain has a single ordering rule so that
merging corpora or runner outputs is commutative, mirroring the merge
semantics the engine already uses. Without a canonical order, the same
corpus could produce different chains and break determinism.

The snapshot is a pointer. A snapshot is a manifest plus a position in the
chain. Time-travel queries reconstruct the state at any past position by
reading the chain prefix up to that position. Determinism of the derived
structures follows from the manifest, the pinned model, and the fixed
segmentation rule, which together form the snapshot contract.

The chain is the source; the projections are the access paths. Observation
requests never scan the whole chain. Each dimension is served by a
projection that is rebuilt from the chain deterministically and
idempotently.

## Derived Projections

Six dimensions feed path weaving over the chain. Each dimension
contributes one kind of hop to an insight path.

| Dimension | Contribution to a path |
|-----------|------------------------|
| Structure | Document and section coordinates from the chain intervals |
| Meaning | Similarity over cell vectors under a pinned model |
| Time | Snapshot positions and change history between builds |
| Provenance | Source file, commit, and build identity per hop |
| Relation | The validated cross-reference graph as derived edges |
| Status | Validity, supersession, and contradiction candidates |

The record model maps the projections onto facts with coordinates and
timestamps. Every path and hop can be traced back to the chain cells and
the snapshot that produced it, which makes the oracle auditable by
construction. Derived rebuilds are idempotent: running the same projection
twice on the same snapshot yields the same index.

The semantic projection deserves one design note. Today meaning depends on
external embedding models, which change over time. The snapshot contract
keeps semantics deterministic by pinning the model and the segmentation
rule to the manifest. A structural vector space, where the vector itself
lives at a coordinate, is the future direction for this projection; until
it exists, external embeddings are permitted only under the pin.

## Recorded Decisions

The following decisions are made in this document and will anchor the
implementation.

- The chain is the primitive source; every index is a derived projection.
- Content is stored once; documents are coordinate intervals over cells.
- The snapshot contract carries determinism: manifest, order rule, pinned
  model, and fixed segmentation.
- The engine and the product are separate layers over one substrate.
- The oracle is defined by the four guarantees of the contract.

## Open Design Questions

Six questions remain open. Each is a decision point for the development
kickoff.

- Cell granularity: token, sentence, or segment, and whether granularity is
  uniform or adaptive.
- Projection cadence: which projections rebuild per snapshot and which
  rebuild lazily on query.
- Semantic introduction: when external embeddings enter under the pin, and
  what the structural vector space must provide to replace them.
- Status detection: how contradiction and supersession detection evolve
  beyond count-based gap heuristics.
- Path semantics: what makes a hop valid across projections and what
  counts as a terminal next step.
- Product surface and distribution: deferred to the decisions recorded in
  the living corpus document.

## Milestones

Phase 1: Snapshot contract. The engine emits a corpus manifest with
document and corpus fingerprints on every build. The evidence criterion is
a manifest that two independent rebuilds reproduce byte for byte.

Phase 2: Chain implementation. The canonical ordering rule, the cell store,
and the structure, time, provenance, and relation projections exist over
one snapshot. The evidence criterion is a time-travel query that returns
the exact state at a past build.

Phase 3: Observation surface. A task entered at a coordinate returns an
insight path with per-hop provenance bound to a snapshot, or an open
intent when no path exists, with semantic projection under the pin. The
evidence criterion is that the four guarantees of the oracle contract hold
on the published corpus.

Phase 4: Scale and governance. Multiple corpora and teams share the
substrate, and each deposit strengthens the shared primitives. The evidence
criterion is a corpus larger than the reference suite managed with the same
guarantees.

Development starts at Phase 1.

## Relationship to Sibling Documents

The four documents form one arc. The index describes what the engine does
today. The single-path artifact pipeline observation describes how corpus
and artifacts converge in one pipeline. The living corpus document states
why the corpus becomes a living knowledge base. This document states how:
snapshot, chain, projections, and oracle. The build pipeline extends into
the oracle pipeline at the snapshot boundary.

## Scope

This document records a design direction. A specification will follow. It
does not describe interfaces, file formats, or implementation details, and
it claims no universal applicability. SDBS is one functional region of the shared
substrate, and its growth follows the ecosystem pattern: each deposit
strengthens the primitives for every other domain.
